en: Odawara to Yumoto: Make Transfers Part of the Day
zh: 小田原到汤本：把换乘放进行程
ja: 小田原から湯本へ：乗り換えを旅程に入れる

p.src: On reaching Odawara, step out of the main flow long enough to check the destination. The Shinkansen, JR local lines, Odakyu, and the Hakone Tozan Line meet in one station, but their gates are not on the same level. On the station plan checked on 16 August 2026, the Shinkansen gate is by the west exit on level 1, while the shared Odakyu and Hakone Tozan gate is on level 3. Use that only to anticipate an upward move; follow current signs rather than memorising a platform. When travelling together, one person can watch the bags while the other confirms the ticket and Hakone-Yumoto direction.

caption.zh: 小田原站内的换乘时刻：四位向导停在检票口外，先确认箱根汤本方向，再带着行李移动。空间说明换乘尺度，不代替当天的站内标识。
caption.ja: 小田原駅での乗り換え。四人のガイドは改札前で箱根湯本方面を確かめてから、荷物と一緒に移動する。乗り換えの空間を伝える場面で、当日の構内表示に代わるものではない。
caption.en: Changing trains at Odawara: the four guides pause outside the gates to confirm the Hakone-Yumoto direction before moving with their luggage. The scene conveys transfer scale; it does not replace current station signs.

p.src: This diagram does not identify the fastest train; it marks the places where a decision is required. From Tokyo, Shinagawa, or western Japan, select a Tokaido Shinkansen service that actually stops at Odawara, because not every train does. From Shinjuku, either use a limited express that runs through to Hakone-Yumoto or make Odawara the place to organise tickets and luggage. The route divides after Yumoto: the mountain train generally serves the Gora side, while buses serve the old road and lake according to the first destination. Decide how the bags will move, then choose the branch. That is more reliable than forcing the day into a clockwise or anticlockwise formula.

caption.zh: 小田原与箱根汤本的入口关系。节点与连线表示交通选择，不按距离或时刻绘制；新干线车次、换乘与运行状态要在出发当天确认。

caption.en: Gateway choices around Odawara and Hakone-Yumoto. Nodes and lines show transport decisions, not distance or time; confirm the Shinkansen stop, connections, and live service on the day.

p.src: Treating Yumoto as only a transfer station misses why it has remained Hakone's threshold. In the Kamakura period, the Yusaka route crossed the mountains from Yumoto towards Mishima. In the early Edo period, the Tokaido ran from Yumoto through Hatajuku. The mountain railway from Yumoto to Gora followed in the Taisho era, adding rail to the old walking routes. Odakyu through-running from Odawara to Hakone-Yumoto began in 1950. Roads and vehicles changed, but Yumoto kept the same practical role: this is where travellers reconsider the gradient, their luggage, and the next direction before entering the mountains.

p.src: As checked on 16 August 2026, the Romancecar takes about 80 minutes from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto and all seats are reserved. It needs a limited-express ticket in addition to the base fare, an IC payment, or a covering pass. The adult surcharge is JPY 1,200 at the station; sales open at 10:00 JST one month before travel. Adult Hakone Freepass prices are JPY 6,000/6,400 for two/three days from Odawara and JPY 7,100/7,500 from Shinjuku; the Romancecar surcharge is extra. List the mountain train, cable car, ropeway, boat, and bus rides you will use, then compare the pass with individual fares.

p.src: When the train stops, the mountains are already visible beyond the station, but the four guides do not chase the next departure. They first separate the day's essentials from the large bag: identification, medicine, rainwear, a power bank, water, and tickets stay close; the overnight case can be delivered, stored, or carried. Yumoto feels like an arrival, yet it is also the last easy place to change the luggage plan before entering the mountains. Deal with the case first, then choose the mountain train or bus from the first attraction and tonight's lodging. The later transfers become easier.

caption.zh: 箱根汤本的进山时刻：山谷和登山电车已经在眼前，四位向导仍先把当天要用的东西从过夜行李中分出来。
caption.ja: 箱根湯本で山へ入る前のひととき。谷と登山電車が目の前にあっても、四人のガイドは宿泊用の荷物から、その日に使う物を先に分ける。
caption.en: The threshold at Hakone-Yumoto: with the valley and mountain train already in view, the four guides still separate the day's essentials from the overnight luggage first.

p.src: Under the Hakone Carry Service terms checked on 16 August 2026, bags are accepted at Yumoto Station from 08:30 to 12:00 for delivery to participating lodgings after 15:00. For the return, leave the bag with a participating lodging by 10:00 and collect it at Yumoto between 13:30 and 18:30. One-way prices are JPY 1,500 up to 140 cm total/15 kg and JPY 2,500 up to 200 cm total/30 kg. Confirm that the lodging participates, then check excluded contents, weather limits, and same-day acceptance. Keep identification, medicine, valuables, and anything needed during the day with you.

p.src: There is no need to declare a clockwise or anticlockwise day before leaving Yumoto. The first place that matters and the lodging district are enough to set the direction. Check the mountain train for Gora or the Open-Air Museum; check the relevant bus for the Hatajuku old road, Moto-Hakone, or the lakeshore. A stay in Miyanoshita or Sengokuhara should likewise be routed from the property's location, not from a desire to complete a loop. Write the first leg and the return on the same page, and keep one alternative that does not depend on the ropeway or boat. Use official same-day information and station signs for platforms, departures, and suspensions.

p.src: If Odawara is reached later than planned, do not try to recover the time by rushing through one attraction. Contact the lodging first and confirm latest check-in, the beginning and end of dinner service, and the final shuttle. If you can no longer reach an included dinner at its stated time, agree on an alternative with the property. When a separate meal is needed, confirm a place still serving in Odawara or Yumoto before climbing; do not stake dinner on an unchecked late-opening restaurant in the mountains. Remove a sightseeing stop, not the margin for check-in, food, and a safe return. The missed place can become the first stop next morning.

p.src: Once the tickets, luggage plan, and route to the lodging all point the same way, the Yumoto transfer is complete. Beyond the station, the mountain railway begins to gain height through a narrow valley. Gora, until now only a name on the map, becomes a real climb outside the window. There is no need to recalculate all of Hakone; protect the first stop and the return margin. The next chapter follows the train to Gora, reading the climb through its windows and deciding where a stop is worth the time.
